findings.headline: Your deposited-item return fee is priced below the market.
findings.body: Your deposited-item return fee ($15 vs a $30 median) sits below the peer 25th percentile. It is a customer-favorable position that peers' published schedules can verify. If the pricing is deliberate, it is worth stating plainly in account marketing.

findings.body: Service-charge income was 59.4 basis points of assets in your latest full-year filing, against a 37.2 bps median for 3,325 same-size credit unions. Pricing changes carry more revenue weight here than for a typical peer, so any change should be modeled against actual incidence.

exec_narrative: Brockport Federal Credit Union is compared with 32 credit unions of similar size in New York that publish fee schedules in the Bank Fee Index. Of 5 rankable lines, four sit inside the middle half of the market and one below it (deposited-item return fee). We would suggest one step: state the below-market deposited-item return fee in account marketing, where peers' published schedules make it verifiable.

context_narrative:
Overdraft and returned-item fees have been the focus of regulatory and public attention since 2022, and many of the largest banks have reduced overdraft fees or eliminated NSF fees outright. Community institutions have moved more slowly and more unevenly, which is why the spread inside a peer set is often wider than the headline national averages suggest.

Fee schedules are also now public in a practical sense: they are collected, compared and summarized automatically. A customer or examiner comparing Brockport Federal Credit Union with its peers sees the same published lines this report uses, so the schedule is a positioning document as much as a pricing one.

How to use this report: § 02 shows every line against the peer range; § 03 explains the lines that sit outside it; § 05 names peers line by line. Ranked comparisons require at least eight peers publishing the same line. Where your institution offers several amounts for one category, the report uses the standard consumer charge described in the methodology below.
